newsitem.title: USA: Marsh & McLennan Q2 insurance revenues up.
newsitem.headline: Marsh & McLennan Q2 insurance revenues up.

text.p: Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc said second quarter revenue from its insurance services business rose to $747.7 million from $478.1 million a year ago, reflecting the firm's combination with Johnson & Higgins.
Revenue from Marsh's Putnam investment management business rose to $355.2 million in the second quarter from $265.4 million a year ago.
The Mercer consulting business posted second quarter revenue business of $346.9 million compared with $293.3 million a year ago.

For the first six months of the year, insurance services revenue rose to $1.31 billion from $1.03 billion last year. Investment management revenue rose to $695.8 million from $503.7 million and consulting revenue rose to $652.3 milion from $570.2 million.
"We are pleased with our performance," Marsh & McLennan chairman A.J.C. Smith said in a news release.
"In addition to achieving double-digit growth in earnings, we have made excellent progress integrating our risk and insurance services and consulting businesses with Johnson & Higgins," he said.
"Putnam continued its superb performance, with assets under management rising to $207 billion and revenue growing 34 percent," he said.
"Mercer continued its double-digit revenue growth. We are confident about our prospects for each of our businesses," he said.
